title: Desk Police
logline: The Desk Police raid an open-plan office, confiscating muffins desk by desk, until the officer's detector reaches the one desk that passes inspection: {{product.name}} gets a salute.

avoid: weapons, knives or anything a police parody should never salute

lore: Pellwick & Co is a mid-sized freight logistics firm; the third floor is the 22-person dispatch team, who move about 4,000 pallets a week and run on snacks.
Gary in dispatch has brought blueberry muffins every Tuesday for seven years. Today is also Brenda from accounts' 50th, and her pink cake with seven candles is waiting in the break area.

Officer Dolores Vega has served 19 years with the Desk Standards Unit, whose one rule is: nothing on a desk that doesn't pull its weight. In practice that means pastries. 1,208 confiscations, zero warnings, and she has never once saluted anything on a desk.
Theo runs route planning from the desk by the window. He keeps a bonsai juniper, a spotless keyboard and exactly one personal item; he has never been flagged.
The raid starts at 10:42am, eighteen minutes before the cake.

beats.summary: Glass doors burst open: a uniformed officer with a detector wand announces a Desk Police raid.
Rule of three: the office freezes mid-bite, Gary is made to drop his muffin, she marches down the aisle with the evidence tub.
She reaches Theo's desk. The detector hovers over the product and goes quiet with a soft green light. He names it and its benefit.
She lowers her sunglasses and salutes the product.
The detector shrieks: she dives across the break table at a birthday cake while Theo uses the product, unbothered, in the foreground.
The product on his desk; a red CLEARED stamp slams down beside it; tagline.
